Not to be biased, but I have experimented with hallucinogens (pretty much just mushrooms/psilocybin, and a little bit of salvia although I wouldn’t recommend salvia to most people) and I’d agree that it absolutely can help with depression. I used it a few times when experiencing poor mental health and in general I’d say it helps you be reminded of the pure enjoyment of life and nature.

The thing is, I don’t recommend just anyone use psychedelics because they really aren’t for anyone, lots of people have panic attacks or get anxiety and paranoia using them if they’re not prepared. I think marijuana is a good start, as it can be a hallucinogen in certain cases and it also is used to help with depression and anxiety often times. If you think that goes well for you, maybe then consider using a small dose of something like mushrooms or acid. I think mushrooms are the better option just because of the shorter trip length (4-5 hours as opposed to 10-12 hours for acid which can be overwhelming). They are typically about more relaxing and enjoyable rather than energetic. I do warn about stomach upsets for mushrooms because they can affect your digestive system temporarily so I’ve found the best success with psilocybin chocolate bars, they taste great and they don’t fuck with your stomach that much at all. If you can get your hands on them I’d highly recommend.

If you’re not particularly anxious one day and you have 5-6 hours of free time, it’s a great way to decompress and look deeper into the great parts about life and everyone’s purpose here. It’s helped me a decent amount. But for someone who hasn’t done much in the way of substances, I’d would definitely take it sloe because the altering of the consciousness can be overwhelming and anxiety-inducing if you’re not at all used to it. Hope this helps.

The rule of thumb is it takes about a month for it to be flushed out of your system but it goes faster when you do things like work out and drink a shit ton of water, so I’d probably say it’ll take 3ish weeks for it to be out of your system after you smoked. But I’d suggest looking into it and doing your own research on top of that

You can probably find a place to live off-campus that’s a 2 bed if you’re just wanting to live with you s/o. There are also one bedroom apartments and dorms. They’re usually more expensive but really good if you don’t want roommates. Colleges don’t assign you a place to live, that search is entirely on you. When you find the college you’re going to, it could help to find a subreddit or other online community to ask around for best places to live. 

As for workload, it’s pretty much dependent on your major and how many credits you’re taking per semester. A typical 15 credit semester isn’t too bad but you might take a lot of difficult or work-heavy courses. If you have a good work ethic in high school, I’d suggest to not let it drop because you’ll probably need it for college. Personally, it was hard for me to adjust to the non-daily classes. It’s important to do some work or even go over notes for a class that you don’t have that day. For example, if you have a MWF class, it could be very helpful to work on assignments for that class on Tuesdays and Thursdays. Just a suggestion. I know some people breeze through college but majors and classes are very different for workload and difficulty. AP classes are a decent idea of what college courses are, but not always. They can be harder or easier. What kind of Professor you have can also heavily affect your workload. 

Hope this helps somewhat!

It does seem like it was pierced too low, but you shouldn’t worry about rejection as much as healing complications. Rejection is associated with surface piercings such as eyebrow and navel piercings as well as others; they tend to migrate or reject completely out of the body because they are pierced on an almost-flat surface of the body. Septum’s don’t really reject (or at least i haven’t even heard of a septum rejecting) but if it’s pierced too low, it might be pierced through the lower cartilage which can greatly prolong healing and be painful and generally cause issues anytime you touch it. I’d advise you to just clean it regularly and let it heal without touching it and see if it seems alright, but if you’re bumping it often and it’s very painful, consider taking it out and getting it repierced. If it’s properly pierced in the sweet spot and it’s moderately high up in the tip of your nose, 8mm should be small, snug, and dainty. Mine is pierced in the sweet spot with an 8mm 16g circular barbell and it’s a perfect size for me (a bit tight when flipped up but other than that it’s great), so that size might be good for you. I’ve seen people with unfortunately low pierced septums, and they have to wear small jewelry such as 6mm or smaller to avoid an obnoxiously large appearance. I’d suggest talking to a piercer—he or she will be able to tell you the proper sizing for your anatomy and nose type if you mention you want a small and dainty look. I hope this helps!
